text.title: Project-Spec Structure — Worked Examples
text.summary: The canonical project-spec/ tree with the purpose of every file and subdirectory, followed by a same-PR delta example (good and bad) for feature F0042.

section.title: Canonical tree — flat files
section.p: project-spec/ is a directory tree, never a bulk dump. Each subfolder is a routing node with its own AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md.

list.item: project-spec/AGENTS.md — entry routing doc; lists each subdir + flat file with one-line purpose.
project-spec/mission.md — what this project IS, who it is for, what success looks like.
project-spec/glossary.md — domain vocabulary. Every term that appears in code or UI lives here.
project-spec/business-rules.md — invariants the system enforces. Each rule has an id and lists the code path that enforces it.
project-spec/data-model.md — canonical entity list + relationships. Source of truth above the ORM.
project-spec/auth.md — actors, roles, permissions, session model.
project-spec/deploy.md — hosts, services, deploy scripts. Where each surface runs.
project-spec/config-secrets.md — env-var inventory. Each var has source (1Password / env / file) and consumer.
project-spec/non-functional.md — performance, availability, security, accessibility targets.
project-spec/observability.md — logs, metrics, traces. What is emitted, where it lands, alert thresholds.
project-spec/invariants.md — system-wide invariants beyond business-rules (e.g. "every API response is JSON; no HTML errors").
project-spec/domain/ — per-aggregate or per-bounded-context detail. Each subdir under domain/ is one aggregate.
project-spec/api/ — public contracts (REST endpoints, GraphQL schema, CLI commands). Per-surface subdirs.
project-spec/integrations/ — third-party systems we depend on. One file per integration: contract, failure mode, retry policy.
project-spec/decisions/ — ADR-style records. One file per decision, append-only.

example.code: .aidocs/project-spec/ ├── AGENTS.md CLAUDE.md ├── mission.md glossary.md business-rules.md ├── data-model.md auth.md deploy.md ├── config-secrets.md non-functional.md observability.md ├── invariants.md ├── domain/ AGENTS.md CLAUDE.md <aggregate>/... ├── api/ AGENTS.md CLAUDE.md <surface>/... ├── integrations/ AGENTS.md CLAUDE.md <integration>.md └── decisions/ AGENTS.md CLAUDE.md <nnn>-<decision>.md
example.note: Committed to git. Current revision only — history lives in git and in features/done/.

Feature F0042 adds an email-verification flow. The PR contains code changes + new lines under project-spec/auth.md ("email verification required for tier ≥ solo") + new entry in project-spec/business-rules.md ("BR-019: unverified accounts cannot upgrade tier").
Feature F0042 ships email verification; project-spec/auth.md still describes the pre-feature state. Reviewer approves because "the spec PR is coming next week".

list.item: The rebuild test in 04-procedure step 6 turns "we just know how it works" into a concrete assumption list; every assumption that maps to real-code reality is a gap to close in the same PR or as a CR.
Reviewing the spec diff against the code diff (step 5) catches the author's blind spot — both were written from the same mental model.
